"Stuffy" has three main meanings. What's beautiful about this word is that a single idea quietly connects all three: the feeling of something being closed off, blocked, or airless.
Meaning 1: A Room or Place with Bad Air

This is the most common meaning. A stuffy room is one where the air feels warm, heavy, and stale — almost like the air hasn't moved in a long time. You might feel uncomfortable, slightly breathless, or even a headache coming on. It's the opposite of a fresh, well-ventilated space.

This happens when:

  • Windows and doors have been shut for a long time
  • Too many people are packed into a small space
  • There is no fan, air conditioning, or airflow

Examples:

  • "It's so stuffy in here. Can we open a window?"
  • "The old library was stuffy and smelled like dust."
  • "After hours on the plane, the cabin felt unbearably stuffy."

Synonyms for this meaning: airless, close, stifling, muggy, unventilated.

When you have a cold, flu, or allergies, your nose gets congested — filled with mucus — and you can't breathe through it easily. In this state, your nose is described as stuffy.

This is one of the most common expressions in everyday English, especially in informal speech. You'll almost always hear this as "a stuffy nose".

Examples:

  • "I woke up with a stuffy nose and a sore throat."
  • "She couldn't smell anything because of her stuffy nose."
  • "This cold medicine relieves a stuffy nose within minutes."

Synonyms for this meaning: blocked, congested, bunged up (informal British English).
Meaning 3: A Person Who Is Too Formal, Rigid, or Old-Fashioned

This is perhaps the most interesting meaning. When used to describe a person, organization, attitude, or environment, "stuffy" means overly serious, stiff, conventional, and resistant to anything casual, fun, or new.

A stuffy person:

  • Follows rules and traditions very strictly
  • Disapproves of behavior they find too casual, modern, or relaxed
  • Is easily offended by jokes, informality, or anything unconventional
  • Tends to be boring or self-important
  • Often makes others feel uncomfortable or judged

This word carries a mildly critical or mocking tone. When you call someone stuffy, you're gently (or not so gently) criticizing them for being uptight and old-fashioned.

Examples:

  • "My uncle is so stuffy — he insists on wearing a tie even at family barbecues."
  • "The board of directors is too stuffy to consider any new ideas."
  • "She left the stuffy law firm to join a creative startup."
  • "I found the dinner party a bit stuffy — nobody laughed or relaxed."

Synonyms for this meaning: prim, pompous, stiff, strait-laced, conservative, uptight, conventional.

Notice how all three meanings share a core idea — something is closed, blocked, or unable to breathe freely:

  • A stuffy room is sealed off from fresh air.
  • A stuffy nose is physically blocked.
  • A stuffy person is mentally closed — blocked from new ideas, humor, and ease.

This connection is what makes "stuffy" such an expressive and memorable word.

"Stuffy" is moderately negative in all its meanings, but it's never harsh or rude. It's more of a gentle complaint or mild criticism. You'd use it comfortably in everyday conversation, whether talking about the weather, your health, or someone's personality.
